examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
MSTs minimize total spanning-tree weight, not source distances. Distinct edge weights guarantee uniqueness, but uniqueness can also occur with ties. A unique lightest edge across a cut belongs to every MST; an edge tied for lightest can belong to some. A unique heaviest edge on a cycle belongs to no MST. Additive shifts preserve MST ordering because all trees have V−1 edges.

**Key relationship:** An MST has V−1 edges; Kruskal time typically O(E log E)

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Sort or identify cuts/cycles.
2. Contract lighter components before counting equal-weight choices.
3. Distinguish some-MST from every-MST statements.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Use cut/cycle properties, carefully handling equal weights. An edge can belong to some MSTs without belonging to all. Count Kruskal alternatives after contracting lighter-edge components. An MST minimizes total tree weight, not every pairwise path distance.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A triangle has edge weights 1,2,2. How many minimum spanning trees exist?

**Answer: 2.** A tree uses two edges. Pairing weight 1 with either weight 2 gives total 3. Using both weight-2 edges gives 4. Exactly two distinct edge sets are minimum.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Adding the same constant to every edge preserves MST ordering since all spanning trees have |V|−1 edges. It can change shortest paths.

Negative edge weights are allowed in MST problems.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

In a triangle with weights 1,2,3, the MST total is:

- **A.** 6
- **B.** 3
- **C.** 4
- **D.** 5

**Answer: B.** Choose weights 1 and 2, connecting all vertices without a cycle; total=3.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** Distinct weights guarantee a unique MST
- **B.** An MST is always a shortest-path tree
- **C.** Every spanning tree has V edges
- **D.** Adding a constant to all edges preserves the set of MSTs

**Answer: A, D.** Trees have V−1 edges, not V. Distinct weights guarantee uniqueness, and uniform shifts add the same constant to every tree. MST and shortest-path objectives differ.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

A triangle has edge weights 2,2,2. Number of MSTs?



**Answer: 3.** Any pair of the three edges forms a spanning tree of total four. There are choose(3,2)=3.

#### Pattern 4 · NAT · Transfer problem

Every edge of the complete graph K₄ has weight one. Number of minimum spanning trees?



**Answer: 16.** All spanning trees have three edges and equal weight. Cayley's formula gives n^(n−2)=4²=16 labelled spanning trees. Counting only star shapes would miss valid paths.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2024 CS1 · Q34 · NAT

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/minimum-spanning-trees?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Minimum spanning trees: Kruskal and Prim. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Cayley’s formula counts labelled spanning trees of the complete graph Kn as n^(n−2).
2. Here n=4, so the count is 4²=**16**. Equivalently, four labelled stars plus twelve labelled paths give sixteen trees.
3. The vertices are labelled, so differently labelled paths must not be identified.

#### GATE 2024 CS2 · Q51 · MSQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/minimum-spanning-trees?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Minimum spanning trees: Kruskal and Prim. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Fix a cycle and a spanning tree containing all its edges except one edge e. Adding e makes that cycle; removing any other cycle edge f gives another spanning tree.
2. Both trees have even weight, so w(e)−w(f) must be even. Every pair of edges in the cycle therefore has the same parity, proving D.
3. Cycles need not be all even: an all-odd triangle has only even-weight spanning trees. Nor must all graph edges share parity: a tree with weights 1,1,2 has even total weight. A,B,C are not universal. Select **D**.
